## Key Takeaways


- Dr. Ahmed Aljazea’s journey includes twelve years in technical/business roles and twelve years in governance/organizational transformation.
- As Excellence Director, he shifted from identifying problems to creating solutions, embedding improvement into organizational practices.
- His involvement in Qiddiya reflects how governance and digital architecture can create connected environments for complex projects.


My professional journey has been shaped by two defining chapters:


1. Twelve years immersed in technical and business development roles.
2. Twelve years dedicated to governance, systems, and organizational transformation.


Together, these experiences built the foundation for how I approach complex challenges today, through structure, clarity, and intelligent system design.


### **The transition between these two phases marked a pivotal moment in my career.**


I was leading the Business Administrative Department at Najran University, working closely on operational management, process improvement, and organizational performance. It was during this period I received a call from Parsons about an opportunity that would redefine my professional trajectory. I took the leap and joined as a Senior Risk Manager, stepping into a role that required not only technical expertise, but also the ability to bring structure and foresight into highly complex environments.


### **That role became the starting point of my broader transformation.**


As I immersed myself in risk management, I began to see patterns such as recurring challenges that were not just about risk, but about how organizations structure decisions, manage information, and operate as systems. Risk, in many ways, was only a symptom. The real opportunity was deeper: building frameworks that allow organizations to anticipate, adapt, and perform consistently.


### **A realization that shaped my next step.**


Moving into the role of Excellence Director, I shifted my focus from identifying problems to systematically identifying solutions for them. I worked on redefining how:


- Performance is measured.
- Processes are designed.
- Organizations can operate with consistency at scale.


It was not about isolated improvements, but about creating an environment where improvement becomes embedded in the way people work. Over time, this translated into measurable outcomes like faster processes, clearer structures, and stronger alignment across teams.


Yet, the most defining chapter of my journey came when governance and technology began to converge.


“Today, as Senior Manager – Permitting Governance and Systems, I operate at the intersection of information technology and governance, where systems are not just tools, but the backbone of how decisions are made and executed.”


The challenge was no longer about improving processes; it was about designing end-to-end ecosystems that bring together workflows, data, approvals, and compliance into one coherent structure.


In this role, I have been leading the development of digital permitting frameworks, transforming traditionally fragmented processes into structured, system-driven environments. What once relied on manual coordination and individual judgment is now increasingly governed through integrated platforms, automated workflows, and data-driven insights.


### **Impact that extends beyond a single function.**


Building on this experience, I became involved in shaping governance and digital architecture across Qiddiya, one of Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 projects comprised of multiple entertainment facilities including a Six Flags theme park, contributing to how systems, services, and institutional structures come together at a broader level – a connected environment where governance, technology, and operations function as one.


### **A shift to engineering systems of performance.**


“Each role added a layer of understanding, ultimately shaping a perspective that sees organizations not as separate functions, but as interconnected systems.”


Throughout this journey, continuous development has remained a key priority. Completing the Parsons Project Manager Development Program (PMD) further strengthened my ability to lead complex, multi-dimensional initiatives.


Looking back, the path may appear linear, from risk to excellence to governance and systems, but in reality, it has been a process of continuous learning and refinement.


##### About The Author


Dr. Ahmed Aljazea is a technology-driven governance leader specializing in data analytics, digital transformation, and risk management. He holds a PhD in Management Science from the University of Kent, an MBA from King Abdulaziz University, and a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science from King Saud University, alongside PMP, RMP, GRCP, CRMP, PSP, and Lean Six Sigma Black Belt credentials.
